_help: One entry per author, keyed by the name shown on the site (spelling variants are merged in author-names.json).

BIOS (shown ONLY on the author's own page): "bio" is 1-3 sentences written by hand, in our own words, from the page(s) in "bioSources". "bioStatus" is one of: "WikiShia" (bio from the author's WikiShia article, shown), "other source" (from Wikipedia or another reliable source, shown), "from our data only" (no bio: the page shows only the line built from the catalogue), "needs review" (nothing shown until you approve: copy "draftBio" into "bio", or write your own, and set "bioStatus" to "WikiShia" or "other source"). "bioNote" explains doubts. To remove a bio, set "bio": null and "bioStatus": "from our data only". Note: WikiShia publishes no open licence, so never copy its wording; short factual summaries with a source link are fine.

PHOTOS come ONLY from Wikimedia Commons, under a free licence (public domain, CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA), and each is shown with its credit and licence. "photo" is the small copy (lists, cards); "photoLarge" the big portrait on the author's page (never enlarged; "lowRes": true means the original is under 480px wide). To REMOVE a photo set "photo": null and rebuild. To ADD one, put the Wikipedia article title in "wikipedia", then run: node scripts/fetch_author_photos.mjs
Authors with no photo get a navy-and-gold badge with their initials.

neverPhoto: the Prophet, the Imams, Lady Fatima and other members of the Ahlul-Bayt and holy figures, including books attributed to them. They NEVER get a photo or any picture, and are never searched for. The site enforces this even if a photo is added by mistake. Their bios are left for you to write.

FOCUS: "focus" {x, y} is where the face is in the photo, in percent from the left and from the top (set by checking each photo by eye). Every size of the photo is cropped around this point. If a face looks cut off, nudge these numbers and rebuild. Optional "zoom" (e.g. 1.5) enlarges the photo around the face in the small round badges only, for photos taken from far away.

Murtaza Mutahhari.creator: varesoon.ir
Murtaza Mutahhari.bio: Ayatollah Murtaza Mutahhari (1920–1979) was a prominent Shia jurist, philosopher, theologian and writer of the 20th century. A student of Allama Tabataba'i and Imam Khomeini, he was one of the most influential Iranian clerics in explaining Islamic teachings for his time.

Ali Shariati.creator: Unknown author
Ali Shariati.bio: Dr. Ali Shari'ati (1933–1977) was an Iranian Shia intellectual whose ideas influenced the Islamic Revolution of 1979. His lectures at Husayniyya Irshad and at universities between 1968 and 1976 were later published in 36 volumes.

Muhammad Baqir al-Sadr.creator: علي شارف
Muhammad Baqir al-Sadr.bio: Ayatollah Sayyid Muhammad Baqir al-Sadr (1935–1980) was an Iraqi Shia jurist, Quran commentator, thinker and political activist. He studied in Najaf under Ayatollah al-Khoei and others, completed his studies before the age of 20, and went on to teach at the Najaf seminary.

Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai.creator: Unknown author
Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai.bio: Allama Sayyid Muhammad Husayn Tabataba'i (1904–1981) was one of the most influential Shia scholars of 20th-century Iran, an expert in philosophy, Quranic commentary and mysticism. He wrote the Quran commentary al-Mizan, and his students included Mutahhari, Jawadi Amuli and Beheshti.

Imam Khomeini.description: Supreme Leader of Iran from 1979 to 1989
Imam Khomeini.creator: Different
Imam Khomeini.bio: Imam Sayyid Ruhollah Musavi Khomeini (1902–1989) was one of the most important Shia marja's of the 20th century and the leader of the 1979 Islamic Revolution in Iran. Exiled by the Pahlavi government, he spent 13 years teaching and writing in Najaf before returning to Iran.

Ali Khamenei.bio: Ayatollah Sayyid Ali Husayni Khamenei (1939–2026) was the second Leader of the Islamic Republic of Iran and a Shia marja'. Before the revolution he was imprisoned and exiled for opposing the Pahlavi government; afterwards he served two terms as president (1981–1989) and led Friday prayers in Tehran.

Ahmed Deedat.bio: Indian-born South African author and speaker on comparative religion (1918–2005), known for his public debates and booklets on Islam and Christianity.

Muhammad Husayni Beheshti.creator: Unknown author
Muhammad Husayni Beheshti.bio: Ayatollah Sayyid Muhammad Husayni Beheshti was a leading cleric of the Islamic Revolution of Iran who studied in Qom under Ayatollah Burujirdi, Imam Khomeini and Allama Tabataba'i. Unusually for a cleric of his time, he also studied at university and knew English and German, and he helped found the Haqqani School in Qom.

He studied in Mashhad, Qom and Najaf under teachers including Ayatollah Burujirdi and Ayatollah al-Khoei, and became a leading religious authority after al-Khoei's death in 1992.

Husayn Ansariyan.bio: Husayn Ansariyan (born 1944) is an Iranian Shia writer and preacher. His works cover the Quran, hadith, mysticism, ethics and the lives of the Ahl al-Bayt, and include his own writings, translations and lectures.

Murtada al-Askari.bio: Allama Sayyid Murtada al-Askari (1914–2007) was a Shia scholar known for his research into early Islamic history and hadith. His works include Ma'alim al-madrasatayn and 'Abd Allah ibn Saba' and Other Myths.

Ayatollah Hossein Vahid Khorasani.bio: Grand Ayatollah Husayn Vahid Khorasani is a Shia marja' in Qom and a former student of Ayatollah al-Khoei. Educated in Nishapur, Mashhad and Najaf, he teaches advanced jurisprudence at the Qom seminary, where his lectures are among the most widely attended.

Muhaddith Qummi.creator: Unknown author
Muhaddith Qummi.bio: Shaykh Abbas Qummi (1877–1941), known as Muhaddith Qummi, was a prominent Shia scholar of hadith, history and preaching. His best-known works are Mafatih al-jinan, Safinat al-bihar and Muntaha al-amal.

Abdul Husayn Dastghaib Shirazi.bio: Ayatollah Sayyid Abd al-Husayn Dastghaib (1913–1981) was a Shia jurist and the Friday prayer leader of Shiraz, Iran.

Abbasali Amid Zanjani.bio: Abbas Ali Amid Zanjani (died 2011) was an Iranian Shia jurist and writer. His best-known work is a ten-volume collection on Islamic political jurisprudence (Fiqh-i siyasi).

Sherwood Eddy.description: American Protestant missionary, administrator and educator
Sherwood Eddy.creator: Pensées de Pascal
Sherwood Eddy.imageDescription: Visage de Sherwood Eddy tiré de la photo File:G. Sherwood Eddy & Sun Yat-Sen in Canton.jpg
Sherwood Eddy.bio: American Protestant missionary, administrator and educator (1871–1963) who wrote many books and worked across Asia and the Middle East.

Sultanul-Waizin Shirazi.creator: Unknown author
Sultanul-Waizin Shirazi.bio: Sultan al-Wa'izin Shirazi, Sayyid Muhammad Musawi Shirazi (1897–1971), was a Shia scholar and preacher famous for his sermons and debates. His book Peshawar Nights (Shab-ha-yi Pishawar) records his debates with Sunni scholars.

Abdul Hadi al-Fadhli.skipped: the article has no free main image

Allamah Ali Naqi Naqvi.skipped: the article has no free main image
Allamah Ali Naqi Naqvi.bio: Indian Shia scholar, jurist, poet and writer (1905–1988) who wrote many books in Urdu and Arabic, including Shaheed-e-Insaniyat (The Martyr for Mankind).

Allamah Rasheed Turabi.creator: Arsalanrkazi (talk) (Uploads)
Allamah Rasheed Turabi.bio: Allama Rasheed Turabi (1908–1973) was a Shia scholar, orator, poet and philosopher from the Indian subcontinent, later based in Pakistan.

Syed Jawad Naqvi.skipped: image is not on Wikimedia Commons
Syed Jawad Naqvi.bio: Allama Syed Jawad Naqvi is a Pakistani Shia scholar and preacher, founder of the Jamia Urwat-ul-Wusqa seminary in Lahore.

Zafar Bangash.bio: Journalist and commentator (born 1950) based in Toronto, Canada. He is director of the Institute of Contemporary Islamic Thought.

Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian.description: Indian religious leader and founder of the Ahmadiyya community (1835–1908)
Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian.creator: Unknown
Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian.imageDescription: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad (13 February 1835 – 26 May 1908), a religious figure from India, and the founder of the Ahmadiyya movement.
Mirza Ghulam Ahmad of Qadian.bio: Indian religious leader (1835–1908) who founded the Ahmadiyya movement.

Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq.bioNote: Holy figure. Please write or approve this description yourself. No picture is ever shown.

Muhammad Baqir al-Majlisi.bio: Allama Muhammad Baqir al-Majlisi (1627–1699), known as the Second Majlisi, was one of the most famous Shia scholars of hadith and jurisprudence. He compiled the vast hadith collection Bihar al-anwar and wrote many works in Persian for general readers.

Muhammad Mahdi al-Asifi.bio: Ayatollah Muhammad Mahdi al-Asifi (1938–2015) was a Shia scholar and mujtahid of the Najaf seminary and a political activist in Iraq. He wrote on jurisprudence, Quranic commentary, philosophy and social questions, and lived for many years in Iran and Kuwait before returning to Iraq.

Muhammad Mahdi al-Naraqi.bio: Muhaqqiq Muhammad Mahdi Naraqi (1715–1795) was an 18th-century Shia scholar who studied in Iraq under Wahid Bihbahani and Yusuf al-Bahrani. His best-known work is Jami' al-sa'adat, a book on ethics.

S. V. Mir Ahmed Ali.draftBio: Translator of the Quran into English, with a commentary.
S. V. Mir Ahmed Ali.bio: Indian Shia scholar and religious leader (1902–1976), known for his English translation and commentary of the Holy Quran.

Sayyid Muhammad Rizvi.bio: Shia scholar who serves as imam of the Islamic Shia Ithna'asheri Jamaat in Toronto, Canada, and the son of Sayyid Saeed Akhtar Rizvi. His books explain Islamic law and belief.

Shaykh al-Saduq.bio: Shaykh al-Saduq (died 991), Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, was one of the greatest Shia hadith scholars of the 10th century. He compiled Man la yahduruhu al-faqih, one of the Four Books of Shia hadith, and some 300 works are attributed to him.

Zeinolabedin Rahnema.draftBio: Iranian writer, author of Payambar (The Messenger), a life of the Prophet in several volumes; he was nominated for the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Zeinolabedin Rahnema.bioNote: Only passing mentions were found; the Payambar attribution comes from our catalogue.

al-Muhaqqiq al-Hilli.bio: Al-Muhaqqiq al-Hilli (1205–1277), Abu l-Qasim Ja'far ibn al-Hasan al-Hilli, was one of the leading Shia jurists of his century and also a poet. His Shara'i' al-Islam became a standard work of Shia law, and al-Allama al-Hilli was among his students.

Muhammad Javad Bahonar.creator: Unknown author
Muhammad Javad Bahonar.imageDescription: Mohammad Javad Bahonar, 77th Prime Minister of Iran
Muhammad Javad Bahonar.bio: Iranian theologian and politician (1933–1981) who briefly served as Prime Minister of Iran in 1981 before he was killed in a bombing.

Imam Zayn al-Abidin.bioNote: Holy figure. Please write or approve this description yourself. No picture is ever shown.

Sayed Hassan Amin.bio: Iranian lawyer and legal scholar (born 1948) who has written widely on Islamic and Iranian law.

Zafar Ishaq Ansari.bio: Pakistani scholar of Islamic studies (1932–2016). He was president of the International Islamic University in Islamabad and director general of its Islamic Research Institute.

Imam Al-Ghazali.bio: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (c. 1058–1111) was a Persian Sunni scholar, jurist, theologian and mystic, one of the most influential thinkers in Islamic history.

Sami Hadawi.bio: Palestinian scholar and author (1904–2004). He is known for documenting land ownership and village records in Palestine before 1948.

Sayyid Mohammad Taqi Hakim.bio: Al-Sayyid Muhammad Taqi al-Hakim (1922–2002) taught at the Najaf seminary and headed its Faculty of Jurisprudence; his best-known work is al-Usul al-'amma li l-fiqh al-muqaran.
Sayyid Mohammad Taqi Hakim.bioNote: WikiShia has an article on this scholar, but I couldn't confirm he wrote 'How to Bridge the Generation Gap'.

Abu Mohammed Al-Hasan Bin Ali Bin Al-Hus.bio: Ibn Shu'ba al-Harrani, al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, was a Shia compiler of hadith. His major work is Tuhaf al-'uqul.

Mullah Muhammad Faidh al-Kashani.bio: Mulla Muhsin Fayd Kashani was a 17th-century Shia philosopher, hadith scholar, Quran commentator and jurist. He studied with Mulla Sadra, Shaykh Baha'i and Mir Damad.

M. Ali Lakhani.bio: Canadian writer, lawyer and editor (born 1955) whose work focuses on metaphysics and the shared principles of the world's wisdom traditions.

Ayatullah Al-Hajj Ash-Shaykh Husain Maza.bio: Ayatollah Husayn Mazahiri (born 1933) is a Shia marja' who teaches advanced jurisprudence at the seminary of Isfahan. He studied in Qom and Isfahan under Imam Khomeini, Ayatollah Burujirdi and Allama Tabataba'i.

Ibn Abi-l-Hadid Muqazzali.bio: Ibn Abi l-Hadid, Abd al-Hamid ibn Hibat Allah (1190–after 1252), was a poet, man of letters and commentator on Nahj al-Balagha. He followed the Shafi'i school in law and the Mu'tazili school in theology.

Basheer Husain Al-Najafy.bio: Grand Ayatollah Shaykh Bashir Husayn al-Najafi (born 1942) is a Pakistani-born Shia marja' based in Najaf, Iraq.
Basheer Husain Al-Najafy.bioNote: WikiShia has an article on this marja', but I couldn't confirm he wrote 'Miracle Birth Of Imam Mahdi'.

S. A. Rahman.bio: Pakistani judge (1903–1979) who served as the fifth Chief Justice of Pakistan.

Ash-Shaykh Abu Jafar Muhammad ibn Ya'Qub.bio: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni (c. 868–941) was one of the greatest Shia hadith scholars and the compiler of al-Kafi, one of the Four Books of Shia hadith.

Abdulaziz Sachedina.bio: Abdulaziz Sachedina (1942–2025) was a scholar of Shia Islam and professor of Islamic Studies who held the IIIT chair at George Mason University in Virginia. He wrote encyclopedia entries on Mahdism, among other topics.

Sayyid Rida Sadr.bio: Ayatollah Sayyid Rida al-Sadr (1921–1994) was a Shia mujtahid, teacher at the Qom seminary and writer of religious books, and the brother of Sayyid Musa al-Sadr.
Sayyid Rida Sadr.bioNote: WikiShia has an article on this scholar, but I couldn't confirm he wrote 'Imam Ali's Life Motto'.

Ibn Shadhan.bio: Ibn Shadhan al-Qummi, Muhammad ibn Ahmad (c. 946–1029), was a Shia jurist and hadith narrator who travelled to Baghdad, Kufa, Ray and Mecca to study with the scholars of his time.

Reza Shah-Kazemi.bio: British author (born 1960) who writes on comparative mysticism, Islamic studies, Sufism and Shi'ism.

Shaykh 'Emadul Deen Abu Jaafar Mohammad.bio: Imad al-Din al-Tabari was an Imami Shia scholar and hadith narrator of the 11th and 12th centuries. His best-known book is Bisharat al-Mustafa li Shi'at al-Murtada.

Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib.bioNote: Holy figure. Please write or approve this description yourself. No picture is ever shown.

Shaykh al-Imam Ibn Taymiya.bio: Ibn Taymiyya, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Halim al-Harrani (1263–1328), was a Hanbali scholar and theologian. His views were disputed by many scholars of his time, and he was imprisoned several times.

Sheikh Tusi.bioNote: The book in the library is by Nasir al-Din Tusi, not Shaykh al-Tusi, so the name may be recorded wrongly; please check.

Fathi Yakan.bio: Lebanese Islamic cleric and writer (1933–2009) from Tripoli who served in the Lebanese parliament.
